discovery: Proposal and realization of coherent control of single electron spins in semiconductor quantum dots as qubits

nominees.name: Jason Petta
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: Loss and DiVincenzo's 1998 proposal showed that the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined quantum dot could serve as a qubit, with exchange coupling providing two-qubit gates. Over the following decade this vision became reality. Petta and co-workers achieved coherent exchange control of two-electron spin states and spin-echo recovery of coherence (2005). Vandersypen and co-workers demonstrated single-shot readout of an individual electron spin and coherent single-spin rotations by electron spin resonance (2004-2006), later extending these to high-fidelity gates in isotopically purified silicon. Together these breakthroughs established the complete toolbox for initializing, manipulating and measuring individual spins in solids, opened a new chapter in mesoscopic and spin physics, and created a leading, CMOS-compatible platform for scalable quantum processors.
